pages.title: Piers
pages.content:
Piers

Six piers, twenty-four minutes

Six piers make the Ushio Line, from Eastmole to Ropewalk, in Calder Bay. The run takes 24 minutes end to end, and every pier has a step-free ramp.

Ushio Line is one harbour ferry on Calder Bay. The water runs from Eastmole to Ropewalk in 24 minutes and calls at six piers in a fixed order. Eastmole is minute 0, Shipyard Steps minute 5, Lantern Point minute 9, Customs Stairs minute 14, Fishmarket Quay minute 19 and Ropewalk minute 24. A single is $3.20 for any of those distances. Children aged 5 to 15 pay $1.60, and children under 5 travel free.

Ticket windows at Eastmole and Customs Stairs are open every day from 05:15 to 23:30. At the other four piers the ticket is sold on board. Every pier has a step-free ramp. The first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40. The last boat leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and reaches Eastmole at 23:34. If weather stops a sailing, the notice is posted at each pier and on the Notices page.

  1. Eastmole0 min
  2. Shipyard Steps5 min
  3. Lantern Point9 min
  4. Customs Stairs14 min
  5. Fishmarket Quay19 min
  6. Ropewalk24 min

Six piers

  1. 0 minEastmoleCommuter terminal, ticket window
  2. 5 minShipyard StepsWorkshops and the technical college
  3. 9 minLantern PointHousing, the old light
  4. 14 minCustoms StairsCity centre, Harbour Office, ticket window
  5. 19 minFishmarket QuayMarket, open from 06:00
  6. 24 minRopewalkParks and offices

Minutes from Eastmole. Each pier has a step-free ramp.

Pier to pier, daily

Eastmole

Eastmole is the commuter terminal, minute 0 on the line, and it has a ticket window. The window opens at 05:15, the same hour the crew comes aboard for checks, a ramp test and an engine warm, and it stays open until 23:30. The first boat leaves here at 05:40, then every 20 minutes until the morning peak. From 07:00 to 10:00 boats leave every 15 minutes. Midday, from 10:00 to 16:00, returns to every 20 minutes.

The evening peak, from 16:00 to 19:00, is every 15 minutes again, and after 19:00 the interval is 20 minutes until the last arrival. Yuna Seo runs this window and the window at Customs Stairs. Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper are the boats in service. Slack Water, the relief boat, uses the same pier and the same ramp when it is the boat on the line. Each boat takes 180 passengers and 24 bicycles.

Shipyard Steps

Shipyard Steps is five minutes from Eastmole. The workshops are here, and so is the technical college. There is no ticket window. Buy a paper ticket on board. The ramp is step-free. Oskar Bell, an apprentice, brings a bicycle on every morning peak and rides to Shipyard Steps. Morning peak runs from 07:00 until 10:00, with a boat every 15 minutes. A bicycle is $1.00 added to any ticket, on top of a single, a day pass, a ride from a ten-ride book or a monthly pass.

Each boat carries 24 bicycles. The same step-free ramp used by commuters is the way a bicycle comes aboard. Fog or swell can change a sailing on this pier as on the others. When that happens, the notice is posted at Shipyard Steps and on the Notices page. The minutes from Eastmole stay five.

Lantern Point

Lantern Point is nine minutes from Eastmole. Housing stands behind the pier, and the old light marks this part of Calder Bay. Tickets are sold on board. The ramp is step-free. The Lantern Point Year 5 class makes one Tuesday trip across the bay, on the same line and the same fares as any other sailing. A child aged 5 to 15 pays the child single of $1.60. A child under 5 travels free.

An adult single is $3.20 for any distance, including a crossing that uses this pier. The boats in service are Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper, with Slack Water as relief. A Tuesday sailing can be changed by weather. The notice goes up at Lantern Point and on the Notices page. Crew on the boat are the usual four: master, engineer and two deckhands.

Customs Stairs

Customs Stairs is fourteen minutes from Eastmole, at the city centre. The Harbour Office is here: Ushio Line Harbour Office, 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay. The office is open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00. The ticket window is open every day from 05:15 to 23:30. Yuna Seo, pier supervisor, runs this window and the Eastmole window. Dana Whitfield, a night nurse, takes the first boat home from Customs Stairs, the 05:40 from Eastmole, which reaches the stairs at 05:54.

Lost property is asked for at Customs Stairs, at the window or at the office. The phone is +1 555 0142 and the email is hello@ushioline.example. From 10:00 to 16:00 the boats run every 20 minutes. A day pass bought here is $8.50 and lasts until the last boat. The ramp is step-free, and a deckhand takes the paper ticket at the gangway.

Fishmarket Quay

Fishmarket Quay is nineteen minutes from Eastmole. The market opens at 06:00. Leila Rahimi, a fish seller, is first at Fishmarket Quay with her cart on the ramp. The ramp is step-free, one ramp at every pier, so the cart meets the deck on the level. Tickets are sold on board. A single from this quay costs $3.20, the same as a single from any other pier, because the fare is for any distance on the line.

When the ramp is under repair, the notice is the Fishmarket Quay ramp notice, posted at the pier and on the Notices page. Weather is posted the same way. The first boat of the day has left Eastmole at 05:40, and this pier is minute 19 on that line. Bicycle space, if a rider brings one, is $1.00 and one of 24 places on the boat.

Ropewalk

Ropewalk is twenty-four minutes from Eastmole, the far end of the line, by the parks and offices. Ropewalk was added in 1996. Tickets are sold on board, and the ramp is step-free. The last boat of the day leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and arrives at Eastmole at 23:34. From 19:00 the evening interval is every 20 minutes, after the peak of every 15 minutes that runs from 16:00 to 19:00. A day pass at $8.50 lasts until this last boat.

A monthly pass is $74.00, named to the holder, for the calendar month. A ten-ride book is $27.00 in paper tickets, and unused rides in it stay valid with no expiry. The line opened in 1974 with two boats and four piers. Eastmole, at the other end, was added in 2008. The run between the two ends is the whole line.

See the timetable →

pages.title: Timetable
pages.content:
Timetable

Boats from 05:40 to 23:10

The sailing day starts with crew aboard at 05:15 and ends when the last boat reaches Eastmole at 23:34. Ewa Nowak writes the seasonal timetable, and weather can still change a boat.

A sailing day

  1. 05:15Crew aboardChecks, ramp test, engine warm
  2. 05:40First boatLeaves Eastmole, then every 20 minutes
  3. 07:00Morning peakEvery 15 minutes until 10:00
  4. 10:00MiddayEvery 20 minutes until 16:00
  5. 16:00Evening peakEvery 15 minutes until 19:00, then every 20
  6. 23:10Last boatLeaves Ropewalk, arrives Eastmole 23:34

Weather can change a sailing. Notices go up at each pier and on the Notices page.

Pier to pier, daily

A sailing day, in six marks

The sailing day has six marks, and the timetable uses those marks. At 05:15 the crew is aboard for checks, a ramp test and an engine warm. At 05:40 the first boat leaves Eastmole, and boats then leave every 20 minutes. At 07:00 the morning peak begins and boats leave every 15 minutes until 10:00. At 10:00 midday returns to every 20 minutes and holds that interval until 16:00.

At 16:00 the evening peak begins, every 15 minutes until 19:00, and after 19:00 the gap is every 20 minutes. At 23:10 the last boat leaves Ropewalk and arrives at Eastmole at 23:34. Ticket windows at Customs Stairs and Eastmole stay open from 05:15 to 23:30. The day is the same list of stops the line prints for home and for this page.

Departure pattern by period

Read the timetable by the period you are travelling in. From the first boat at 05:40 until 07:00, boats leave Eastmole every 20 minutes. From 07:00 to 10:00 they leave every 15 minutes. From 10:00 to 16:00 they leave every 20 minutes. From 16:00 to 19:00 they leave every 15 minutes. From 19:00 until the last boat they leave every 20 minutes. The last boat is a fixed sailing from the other end: it leaves Ropewalk at 23:10.

Ewa Nowak, timetable planner, writes the seasonal timetable, and the winter timetable uses this day. The pattern names intervals and the last boat. It does not place a boat's name beside each clock time. Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper are in service, and Slack Water is the relief boat, on these same intervals.

  • First boat to morning peak05:40–07:00Every 20 minutes
  • Morning peak07:00–10:00Every 15 minutes
  • Midday10:00–16:00Every 20 minutes
  • Evening peak16:00–19:00Every 15 minutes
  • Evening19:00 to the last boatEvery 20 minutes
  • Last boatLeaves Ropewalk 23:10Arrives Eastmole 23:34

Minutes from Eastmole

Count the line in minutes from Eastmole. Eastmole is 0 minutes, the commuter terminal, with a ticket window. Shipyard Steps is 5 minutes, by the workshops and the technical college. Lantern Point is 9 minutes, by the housing and the old light. Customs Stairs is 14 minutes, at the city centre, with the Harbour Office and a ticket window. Fishmarket Quay is 19 minutes, and the market there opens at 06:00.

Ropewalk is 24 minutes, by the parks and offices. End to end is 24 minutes. The last published times of the day are stated from Ropewalk: departure 23:10, arrival at Eastmole 23:34. A relief sailing on Slack Water uses these same piers and these same minutes. Fares do not change with the length of the ride. A single is $3.20 any distance.

  • EastmoleCommuter terminal, ticket window0 min
  • Shipyard StepsWorkshops and the technical college5 min
  • Lantern PointHousing, the old light9 min
  • Customs StairsCity centre, Harbour Office, ticket window14 min
  • Fishmarket QuayMarket, open from 06:0019 min
  • RopewalkParks and offices24 min

Seasonal timetable and weather

Boats are set to sail every day of the year except when weather stops the service. Fog or swell can change a sailing. The timetable is the plan, and the plan yields when the water requires it. Ushio Line posts that change at each pier and on the Notices page. Ewa Nowak writes the seasonal timetable, including the winter timetable, against the day printed here: crew aboard at 05:15, first boat at 05:40, 15 minutes through each peak, 20 minutes outside the peaks, last boat from Ropewalk at 23:10.

Office hours for a question about the timetable are Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00, at Ushio Line Harbour Office, 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay. Email hello@ushioline.example or call +1 555 0142. Window staff have the same notices from 05:15.

See the fares →

pages.title: Fares
pages.content:
Fares

Paper ticket, or a pass

Fares are in US dollars on every language of this site. A single covers any distance on the one line, and a bicycle is $1.00 on top of any ticket.

Ways to pay

  1. WindowEastmole and Customs StairsOpen every day, 05:15–23:30
  2. On boardThe other four piersShipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Fishmarket Quay, Ropewalk
  3. Harbour Office1 Customs StairsMonday to Saturday, 08:00–18:00

Prices are in US dollars on every language of this site.

Pier to pier, daily

The fare list

A single is $3.20 and covers any distance on the line, one pier or the full run from Eastmole to Ropewalk. A child single is $1.60 for ages 5 to 15. Children under 5 travel free. A day pass is $8.50 and lasts until the last boat. A ten-ride book is $27.00, paper tickets, with no expiry. A monthly pass is $74.00 for the calendar month and is named to the holder.

A bicycle is $1.00 added to any ticket. Each boat carries 180 passengers and 24 bicycles. Ticket windows at Customs Stairs and Eastmole sell these fares every day from 05:15 to 23:30. At Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk the same fares are sold on board. Prices are in US dollars on every language of this site. The list below is the fare list of the line.

  • SingleAny distance on the line$3.20
  • Child singleAges 5–15; under 5 travel free$1.60
  • Day passUntil the last boat$8.50
  • Ten-ride bookPaper tickets, no expiry$27.00
  • Monthly passCalendar month, named$74.00
  • BicycleAdded to any ticket$1.00

Where to buy

Ways to pay are the paper ticket and the named pass. At Eastmole and at Customs Stairs, use the ticket window. Yuna Seo, pier supervisor at Customs Stairs, runs both windows. The windows open at 05:15, when the crew comes aboard, and close at 23:30. The last boat arrives at Eastmole at 23:34. At Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk, pay on board and take a paper ticket.

A single is one ride. A day pass covers the rest of that sailing day until the last boat. A monthly pass covers the named calendar month. A ten-ride book covers ten rides on paper. The Harbour Office at 1 Customs Stairs is open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00, for a question about a pass. The phone is +1 555 0142 and the email is hello@ushioline.example.

Paper tickets

A paper ticket is the ordinary way onto the boat. The deckhand takes it at the gangway. A single at $3.20 is one ride, any distance among the six piers. Keep a day pass with you until the last boat, the sailing that leaves Ropewalk at 23:10. A monthly pass is named, so it is held by the person named on it, for that calendar month, at $74.00. A ten-ride book is paper, at $27.00.

Bring the paper with you each time you ride. A bicycle is not included in the ticket price. Add $1.00 for the bicycle, and it takes one of the 24 bicycle spaces on that boat. Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake, Sandpiper and the relief boat Slack Water all use this same ticket. The ramp is step-free at every pier where the ticket is taken.

Concessions

The published concession is the child fare. Ages 5 to 15 pay $1.60 for a single, any distance on the line. Under 5, the child travels free. The day pass at $8.50, the ten-ride book at $27.00 and the monthly pass at $74.00 are the prices printed for those tickets. The Lantern Point Year 5 class, on its one Tuesday trip across the bay, uses these fares.

A bicycle on a child's ticket is still $1.00. Oskar Bell's bicycle on the morning peak to Shipyard Steps is the same bicycle charge, added to the ticket he holds. Window staff at Customs Stairs and Eastmole sell the child single during the ordinary window hours, every day from 05:15 to 23:30. On board, the other four piers sell it too.

Ten-ride tickets

Unused ten-ride tickets stay valid, with no expiry. An unused ride in the book remains a ride. The book costs $27.00 and it is paper. It is a book of rides, separate from the monthly pass. The monthly pass is $74.00, named, and it covers one calendar month. The day pass is $8.50 and it ends with the last boat. Buy a book at the ticket windows of Customs Stairs and Eastmole, or on board at Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk.

If the book is given a new cover, the Notices page carries that notice. The validity line stays the one printed here. For a question about a book, the Harbour Office is open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00, at 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay, on hello@ushioline.example and +1 555 0142.

How to board →

pages.title: The Boats
pages.content:
The Boats

Five boats

Five boats work the Ushio Line. Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper are in service, and Slack Water is the relief boat.

Specifications

  1. 180PassengersOn every boat
  2. 24BicyclesAt $1.00 added to any ticket
  3. 1Step-free rampAt every pier
  4. 4CrewA master, an engineer, two deckhands

The same figures for all five boats.

Pier to pier, daily

Every boat, the same figures

Each boat on Ushio Line is published to the same figures. The passenger capacity is 180. The bicycle space is 24. Boarding is by a step-free ramp, at Eastmole, Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Customs Stairs, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk. A sailing carries four crew: a master, an engineer and two deckhands. The line they keep is 24 minutes from Eastmole to Ropewalk. The first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40, after the crew has been aboard from 05:15 for checks, a ramp test and an engine warm.

The last boat leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and arrives at Eastmole at 23:34. When weather stops the service, the notice is posted at each pier and on the Notices page. Fares on every boat are the same published fares, beginning at $3.20 for a single.

Built, and in service

  • 2011Morning TernIn service. Master Ruth Adeyemi.
  • 2011PetrelIn service. Deckhand Mateus Carvalho.
  • 2014KittiwakeIn service.
  • 2014SandpiperIn service.
  • 1998Slack WaterRelief boat.

Boats in service

Four boats are in service. Morning Tern was built in 2011. Ruth Adeyemi is master of Morning Tern and joined in 2009. Petrel was built in 2011. Mateus Carvalho is a deckhand on Petrel and joined in 2021. Kittiwake was built in 2014. Sandpiper was built in 2014. Tomas Lindgren, chief engineer, looks after all five boats, the four in service and the relief boat. Priya Nair, deck lead, trains the deckhands who sail on them.

The timetable gives the intervals of the day and the last boat. It gives the pier minutes. It leaves the day's hull to the working list. All four boats share the ramp, the count of 180 passengers and the count of 24 bicycles. A paper ticket taken at the gangway is the same ticket on each of them.

Relief boat

Slack Water

Slack Water is the relief boat. It was built in 1998. Morning Tern and Petrel were built in 2011. Kittiwake and Sandpiper were built in 2014. Slack Water comes onto the line when a service boat is not sailing. Maintenance on Slack Water is posted as a notice on the Notices page and at the piers. While Slack Water is the boat in use, the sailing remains an Ushio Line sailing.

The six piers stay in order. The run stays 24 minutes. The fares stay the published fares. The ramp stays step-free. The crew stays four. Tomas Lindgren looks after Slack Water with the other four boats. The relief boat is the spare hull for this commuter line. The line was founded in 1974 with two boats. Five boats are on the list now.

Read the notices →

Meet the crew →

pages.title: Crew
pages.content:
Crew

Seven people, one line

Four people run each sailing: a master, an engineer and two deckhands. Seven named people carry the work between the deck, the windows and the Harbour Office.

Four to a sailing

  1. MasterRuth AdeyemiHas the boat
  2. EngineerTomas LindgrenHas the machinery
  3. DeckhandMateus CarvalhoRamp, ropes and paper tickets
  4. DeckhandPriya Nair leads the deckRamp, ropes and paper tickets

Crew come aboard at 05:15. The first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40.

Pier to pier, daily

The crew of four

A sailing leaves the pier with four crew. The master has the boat. The engineer has the machinery. Two deckhands have the ramp, the ropes and the paper tickets at the gangway. Priya Nair, deck lead, trains the deckhands. Tomas Lindgren is chief engineer and looks after all five boats. Ruth Adeyemi is master of Morning Tern. The other boats sail with a master in that same role.

Crew come aboard at 05:15, for checks, a ramp test and an engine warm, before the first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40. The complement stays four on Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake, Sandpiper and, when it is sailing, on Slack Water. Passenger capacity beside that crew is 180, with space for 24 bicycles.

The people

The people of the line

Ruth Adeyemi is master of Morning Tern and joined in 2009. Tomas Lindgren is chief engineer. He looks after Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake, Sandpiper and Slack Water. Priya Nair is deck lead. She trains the deckhands who take tickets, tend the ramp and handle ropes. Mateus Carvalho is a deckhand on Petrel and joined in 2021. Yuna Seo is pier supervisor at Customs Stairs. She runs the ticket window there and the ticket window at Eastmole, every day from 05:15 to 23:30.

  • MasterRuth AdeyemiMorning Tern. Joined 2009.
  • Chief engineerTomas LindgrenLooks after all five boats.
  • Deck leadPriya NairTrains the deckhands.
  • DeckhandMateus CarvalhoPetrel. Joined 2021.
  • Pier supervisorYuna SeoCustoms Stairs. Runs both ticket windows.
  • Timetable plannerEwa NowakWrites the seasonal timetable.
  • General managerSamir HaddadSince 2019.

How a shift runs

The shift starts at 05:15, when the crew comes aboard. The work before the first passenger is checks, a ramp test and an engine warm. At 05:40 the first boat leaves Eastmole. Deckhands take paper tickets at the gangway and attend the step-free ramp. Dana Whitfield, a night nurse, takes the first boat home from Customs Stairs, the 05:40 from Eastmole, which reaches the stairs at 05:54, so the first sailing is already a ride home for someone leaving night work.

Through the morning peak, from 07:00 to 10:00, boats leave every 15 minutes. That is the peak on which Oskar Bell boards with his bicycle for Shipyard Steps. The day continues on the published intervals until the last boat leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and reaches Eastmole at 23:34. Windows stay open until 23:30. If weather stops the remaining sailings, the notice is posted at each pier and on the Notices page.

About the line →

pages.title: On Board
pages.content:
On Board

Step-free at every pier

Boarding is step-free at every pier. A paper ticket is taken at the gangway, and the crew of four has been aboard since 05:15.

Boarding

Level boarding, every pier

Every pier has a step-free ramp. Eastmole, Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Customs Stairs, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk all board on the level. A wheelchair user and a deckhand use that ramp between pier and deck. Leila Rahimi brings her cart onto the ramp at Fishmarket Quay. The ramp is tested at the start of the shift: at 05:15 the crew is aboard for checks, a ramp test and an engine warm.

Each boat has a ramp, the four boats in service and the relief boat Slack Water. A sailing carries 180 passengers and a crew of four. The deckhand at the gangway takes the paper ticket. If fog or swell stops the boat, the notice is posted at the pier and the sailing waits. The first boat, when it goes, leaves Eastmole at 05:40.

Read the fares →

Bicycles

A boat carries 24 bicycles. The bicycle fare is $1.00 added to any ticket. That ticket may be a single at $3.20, a child single at $1.60, a day pass at $8.50, a ride from a ten-ride book at $27.00, or a monthly pass at $74.00. Oskar Bell, an apprentice, brings a bicycle on every morning peak to Shipyard Steps. The morning peak is 07:00 to 10:00, a boat every 15 minutes.

Bring the bicycle onto the step-free ramp. It takes one of the 24 spaces on that sailing. The bicycle fare is the same at every pier, because a ticket is already valid for any distance and the bicycle is only the added $1.00. When the racks change, the Notices page carries the bicycle rack notice. The charge printed here is the charge.

Children

Children aged 5 to 15 pay $1.60 for a single, any distance on the six piers. Children under 5 travel free. The Lantern Point Year 5 class takes one Tuesday trip across the bay on the ordinary boats. They use the same piers, the same ramp and the same sailing day as the rest of the line. A single is the fare for one ride. A day pass, for a day that lasts until the last boat, is $8.50.

Adults pay $3.20. The crew on the class sailing is the usual four: master, engineer and two deckhands. Boats in service are Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper, with Slack Water if the relief boat is the hull that day. Weather can change a Tuesday. The notice is posted at Lantern Point and on the Notices page.

Pets

The fare table has a line for a bicycle and lines for people. It has no separate price for an animal. Questions about a pet on board go to the deckhand at the ramp before boarding, or to the Harbour Office. The office is Ushio Line Harbour Office, 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay, open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00, on hello@ushioline.example and +1 555 0142.

Ticket windows at Customs Stairs and Eastmole are open every day from 05:15 to 23:30, and Yuna Seo runs both. A pet, if it comes, comes with the person who holds the ticket, on the same step-free ramp, inside the sailing's capacity of 180 passengers. The bicycle charge of $1.00 stays the bicycle charge. Ask at the gangway on the day.

Fog, swell and lost property

The line is set to sail every day of the year except when weather stops the service. In fog or swell, read the notice at the pier before you count on the next interval. The same notice is on the Notices page. The crew has been aboard since 05:15. A stopped sailing stays stopped until a notice says it goes. Ticket windows at Eastmole and Customs Stairs can answer during window hours, 05:15 to 23:30.

Lost property is handled at Customs Stairs. Ask at that ticket window, or at the Harbour Office, 1 Customs Stairs, during office hours, Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00. The phone is +1 555 0142 and the email is hello@ushioline.example. Name the pier you boarded and, if you know it, the boat.

Read the notices →

pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

A commuter line, on the water

Ushio Line was founded in 1974 in Calder Bay, with two boats and four piers. Ropewalk was added in 1996 and Eastmole in 2008.

1974 · 1996 · 2008

  1. 1974FoundedTwo boats and four piers on Calder Bay
  2. 1996Ropewalk addedMinute 24, by the parks and offices
  3. 2008Eastmole addedMinute 0, the commuter terminal

Today: six piers, five boats, twenty-four minutes end to end.

Pier to pier, daily

History

Three dates, one line

Ushio Line was founded in 1974 with two boats and four piers, on Calder Bay. Ropewalk was added in 1996. That pier is now minute 24, by the parks and offices. Eastmole was added in 2008. That pier is now minute 0, the commuter terminal, with a ticket window. The line today has six piers and five boats, and the run between the ends is 24 minutes.

Morning Tern and Petrel were built in 2011. Kittiwake and Sandpiper were built in 2014. Slack Water, the relief boat, was built in 1998. Four boats are in service, and Slack Water is relief. Each carries 180 passengers and 24 bicycles. Samir Haddad has been general manager since 2019. The Harbour Office is at 1 Customs Stairs, open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00.

A working morning

Dana Whitfield, a night nurse, takes the first boat home from Customs Stairs, the 05:40 from Eastmole, which reaches the stairs at 05:54. The crew has been aboard since 05:15 for checks, a ramp test and an engine warm. Her pier is the city-centre stop, where the Harbour Office stands at 1 Customs Stairs. Oskar Bell, an apprentice, brings a bicycle on every morning peak and gets off at Shipyard Steps, five minutes from Eastmole, for the workshops and the technical college.

The peak runs from 07:00 to 10:00, every 15 minutes, and the bicycle is $1.00 on his ticket. Leila Rahimi, a fish seller, is first at Fishmarket Quay with her cart on the ramp. The market opens at 06:00. The ramp is step-free. These three are ordinary mornings on a commuter line. The pier is the platform. The water is the line.

One line across the bay

The Lantern Point Year 5 class makes one Tuesday trip across the bay. Lantern Point is nine minutes from Eastmole, the pier by the housing and the old light. The class uses the boats of the line: Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake or Sandpiper, or Slack Water when the relief boat is sailing. They board on the step-free ramp with a crew of four. Around that one Tuesday, the line runs its ordinary day, from the 05:40 out of Eastmole until the last boat leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and arrives at Eastmole at 23:34.

The line opened with two boats and four piers in 1974. It now has five boats and six piers. The use of it is the same kind of use: a short ride, pier to pier, on the days the water allows.

Samir Haddad, general manager since 2019

We set out to sail every day of the year except when weather stops the service.

I have been general manager since 2019. The line I watch was founded in 1974, with Ropewalk added in 1996 and Eastmole added in 2008. We set out to sail every day of the year except when weather stops the service. If fog or swell changes a boat, the notice goes up at each pier and on the Notices page. I keep that sentence plain. The fares stay the published ones: $3.20 for a single, $1.60 for a child aged 5 to 15, free under 5, $8.50 for a day pass until the last boat, $27.00 for a ten-ride book, with unused tickets still valid and no expiry, $74.00 for a named monthly pass, and $1.00 for a bicycle.

The office is at 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay. Write to hello@ushioline.example or call +1 555 0142, Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00. The pier is the platform. The water is the line.

Harbour Office

Ushio Line Harbour Office is at 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay. The office is open Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00. Email hello@ushioline.example. Phone +1 555 0142. Samir Haddad, general manager since 2019, is the manager of the line. Yuna Seo, pier supervisor at Customs Stairs, runs the ticket windows. The office is the place for a question about a named monthly pass, a ten-ride book, the seasonal timetable Ewa Nowak writes, or a notice you cannot see at the pier.

Customs Stairs is fourteen minutes from Eastmole, at the city centre. The tag line of the company is the one used on the boats: harbour ferry, pier to pier. The story line is the same one Samir signs in his note. The pier is the platform. The water is the line.

Ticket windows

Ticket windows are at Customs Stairs and at Eastmole. They are open every day, 05:15 to 23:30, including Sunday, when the office is closed, and including every other day of the year the boats are set to sail. Yuna Seo runs both windows. At Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk there is no window. Buy the ticket on board from the crew. The windows sell the published fares. A single is $3.20.

A child single is $1.60 for ages 5 to 15, and under 5 is free. A day pass is $8.50 until the last boat. A ten-ride book is $27.00, paper, with no expiry on unused tickets. A monthly pass is $74.00, named, for the calendar month. A bicycle is $1.00 added to any ticket. The windows are open at 05:15, when the crew comes aboard. The first boat leaves Eastmole at 05:40.

Lost property

Lost property is handled at Customs Stairs. Ask at the ticket window during window hours, every day from 05:15 to 23:30, or at the Harbour Office during office hours, Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00. The address is 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay. The phone is +1 555 0142 and the email is hello@ushioline.example. Say the pier you boarded. The piers are Eastmole, Shipyard Steps, Lantern Point, Customs Stairs, Fishmarket Quay and Ropewalk.

Say the boat if you know it. The boats in service are Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper. Slack Water is the relief boat. A deckhand is the person who takes a paper ticket at the gangway, one of two deckhands in a crew of four. If weather stopped the sailing, the notice for it is on the Notices page and at the pier.

posts.title: Winter timetable
posts.excerpt: Ewa Nowak's winter timetable sets out the same sailing day for Calder Bay, from crew aboard at 05:15 to the last boat into Eastmole at 23:34.
posts.content:
The winter timetable is the seasonal timetable for Ushio Line, written by Ewa Nowak, timetable planner. It covers the harbour ferry in Calder Bay. The shape of the service is the shape fixed for the line. There is one line, six piers, and 24 minutes from end to end. The pier is the platform. The water is the line. What follows is the day the winter timetable prints.

Crew come aboard at 05:15. The work at the pier is checks, a ramp test and an engine warm. Four people make a sailing: the master, the engineer and two deckhands. Ruth Adeyemi is master of Morning Tern and joined in 2009. Priya Nair, deck lead, trains the deckhands who take paper tickets at the gangway.

Tomas Lindgren, chief engineer, looks after all five boats. At 05:40 the first boat leaves Eastmole. Ticket windows at Eastmole and at Customs Stairs are already open. Yuna Seo, pier supervisor, runs both windows, every day from 05:15 to 23:30.

Dana Whitfield, a night nurse, takes the first boat home from Customs Stairs, the 05:40 from Eastmole, which reaches the stairs at 05:54. Customs Stairs is the city-centre pier, 14 minutes from Eastmole, and the Harbour Office stands there at 1 Customs Stairs. After the first boat, departures from Eastmole continue every 20 minutes until the morning peak. The single she needs is the ordinary single, $3.20, any distance on the line. A day pass, if the day runs on, is $8.50 until the last boat.

At 07:00 the morning peak begins. Boats leave every 15 minutes until 10:00. Oskar Bell, an apprentice, brings a bicycle on every morning peak to Shipyard Steps. Shipyard Steps is 5 minutes from Eastmole, the pier for the workshops and the technical college. A bicycle is $1.00 added to any ticket, and each boat carries 24 bicycles. He pays the published fare for the ticket he holds, plus that $1.00. The peak interval in the winter timetable is the same 15 minutes printed for the rest of the year.

The minutes from Eastmole are the map inside the timetable. Eastmole is 0, the commuter terminal, with a ticket window. Shipyard Steps is 5. Lantern Point is 9, by the housing and the old light. Customs Stairs is 14. Fishmarket Quay is 19, and the market opens at 06:00. Ropewalk is 24, by the parks and offices. Ropewalk was added in 1996. Eastmole was added in 2008. The line was founded in 1974 with two boats and four piers. End to end remains 24 minutes.

Leila Rahimi, a fish seller, is first at Fishmarket Quay with her cart on the ramp. The ramp is step-free, as it is at every pier. From 10:00 the midday pattern runs every 20 minutes until 16:00. A child aged 5 to 15 pays $1.60 for a single. A child under 5 travels free. A named monthly pass is $74.00 and covers the calendar month. None of those prices changes because the timetable is the winter one.

At 16:00 the evening peak begins, every 15 minutes until 19:00. After 19:00 the boats return to every 20 minutes. The last boat leaves Ropewalk at 23:10 and arrives at Eastmole at 23:34. That arrival is the end of the sailing day and the end of a day pass. The windows close at 23:30. The last boat arrives at Eastmole at 23:34.

Four boats are in service. Morning Tern and Petrel were built in 2011. Kittiwake and Sandpiper were built in 2014. Mateus Carvalho is a deckhand on Petrel and joined in 2021. Slack Water, built in 1998, is the relief boat. Each boat carries 180 passengers and has a step-free ramp.

When Slack Water takes a sailing, the winter timetable still applies: the same piers, the same intervals, the same fares and the same crew of four. A notice of Slack Water maintenance is posted when maintenance is the news, at each pier and on the Notices page.

The boats are set to sail every day of the year except when weather stops the service. Fog or swell can change a departure listed in the winter timetable. Ushio Line posts the change at each pier and on the Notices page. The printed intervals are the plan. Samir Haddad, general manager since 2019, keeps that account plain. Riders read the notice on the day.

The Lantern Point Year 5 class still has its one Tuesday trip across the bay under this timetable. It is one crossing on the ordinary line, at the ordinary fares, from the pier at minute 9. Unused ten-ride tickets stay valid, with no expiry, through the season this timetable covers and after it. The book is $27.00 and it is paper. A new cover, when the Notices page announces one, leaves that validity as it stands.

Questions about the winter timetable go to the Harbour Office, Monday to Saturday, 08:00 to 18:00, at 1 Customs Stairs, Calder Bay. Email hello@ushioline.example. Phone +1 555 0142. On the pier, the windows and the deckhands have the day's notice. The winter timetable is a full sailing day on a short line. Harbour ferry, pier to pier.

posts.title: Fishmarket Quay ramp repairs
posts.excerpt: The ramp at Fishmarket Quay is being resurfaced. The pier stays open with a temporary level ramp.
posts.content:
Resurfacing of the Fishmarket Quay ramp takes place over two weeks. The pier stays open, and a temporary step-free ramp is in place.

Leila Rahimi and the other market sellers have been asked to use the east side of the quay while the work is done.

posts.title: Slack Water in maintenance
posts.excerpt: Slack Water, the relief boat, is out for maintenance. The four service boats cover every sailing.
posts.content:
Slack Water, built in 1998, is in the yard for routine maintenance. Morning Tern, Petrel, Kittiwake and Sandpiper cover every sailing.

Tomas Lindgren, chief engineer, expects the boat back in service before the winter timetable begins.

posts.title: New covers for the ten-ride book
posts.excerpt: The ten-ride book has a new cover. The paper tickets inside are unchanged and still have no expiry.
posts.content:
The ten-ride book, $27.00, now has a stiffer cover that fits a coat pocket. The paper tickets inside are the same as before.

Books bought earlier stay valid. There is no expiry on unused tickets.

posts.title: Bicycle racks move to the stern
posts.excerpt: Bicycle racks on all five boats move to the stern deck. Each boat still takes 24 bicycles.
posts.content:
The bicycle racks move to the stern deck on every boat, next to the ramp. Each boat still takes 24 bicycles at $1.00 added to any ticket.

Deckhands will help during the morning peak.

posts.title: Lantern Point Year 5 trip
posts.excerpt: The Lantern Point Year 5 class makes its one Tuesday trip across the bay. Please give them room on the deck.
posts.content:
On Tuesday the Lantern Point Year 5 class makes its trip across the bay on the morning boat. Priya Nair and the deckhands will meet them at the gangway.

Children under 5 travel free and the class travels on a group ticket.
